cells.tense: The scale is here, in your hands, and it is steady now.
cells.act: let the old form go so the next one can come
cells.ask: Let one arrangement that has already run its course end, plainly, with no announcement — and clear the room behind it.
cells.core:
You're being pulled toward something you actually want, and you're carrying it fairly. The people who gave to get you here have what they gave back, in one form or another, and you know the difference between what's owed and what's not. That's the ground the pull is standing on. It doesn't need checking. It runs.

There's a piece of how things are set up that belongs to an earlier version of you — an arrangement, an understanding, a share of something that was fair once and isn't any more. It's already finished. It's still here because closing it takes a plain act and a minute, and those are the things that wait. Close it, accept what that costs, and clear the room. What you're moving toward doesn't need the old shape in the way.
cells.sheetLine: Fairness runs in you, and one thing here is already finished.
cells.verb: to weigh what's owed and give it its true weight
cells.place: the place where something in you is pulling toward what it wants to become

cells.tense: You are adding up what you will be owed before any of it has happened.
cells.act: carry it without tightening around it
cells.ask: Pick one person you're moving alongside, and for a day, carry the weight of what's between you without counting it — no tally, no mental note.
cells.core:
There's a direction you're steering by, and it's a real one. But on the way there, the tracking is running. Who gave what, who'll owe, what you'll get back — the tally turns over in the back of your mind on the walk over. The people you're with can feel the counting rest on them. Nobody's asking you to be careless. The tally has simply grown louder than the care it was there to guard.

There's a kind of strength that carries what's between two people without gripping it. Try that, on one person, for one day. Not a ledger and not a debt — just hold the weight without adding to it, without calling in what's owed. If something's off, you'll see it without having counted. Then it's one thing to answer, instead of arithmetic running every hour. The light you started with stays lit.
cells.sheetLine: The counting is louder than the care.
cells.verb: to weigh what's owed and give it its true weight
cells.place: the place where something in you is pulling toward what it wants to become

cells.tense: The door that closed still has your hand on it, somewhere, even now.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Do the small thing you do alone — same version, same length — today, and keep it even if nothing comes of it.
cells.core:
You can see where you're trying to get, and you're giving more than you're getting back on the way. That's been true for a while, and you've stopped counting it. In this area, asking for what's yours stays hard. The pull is still there. It's just difficult to trust a direction when you're not sure the ground under you will hold.

There's a practice you do alone — a small steady thing, kept by attention. Do it today, all of it, at whatever length is yours, the same way you did it last time. That's how a light comes back: not by being told it matters, but by being kept. Nothing has to be decided about the request you haven't made yet. The repeating is the whole act, and it's enough for today.
cells.sheetLine: You give more than you get, and the practice is the way back.
cells.verb: to weigh what's owed and give it its true weight
cells.place: the place where something in you is pulling toward what it wants to become

cells.tense: You are keeping a tally you would deny keeping, right now.
cells.act: notice what you already know before you reason about it
cells.ask: Before you settle the next question of who owes what here, stop, and take what came to you first, before the arguing starts.
cells.core:
There's something pulling you toward a light you want, and on the way there, you're weighing. You'd say you weren't — that you're not the type to keep score. But the tally is there: small things not returned, chances you didn't get, moments you noticed and filed away. The counting is happening, and your hand on it is out of sight. The counting isn't the problem. Not seeing your hand on it is.

The fix isn't to stop weighing. It's to see the weighing as something you're doing. The next time who-gave-what comes up, don't reason first. Stop, and take what came to you first, before the case you were about to build. That first sense is usually right, and it's usually smaller than the argument. Let it land, and the scale is back in view.
cells.sheetLine: The tally is yours. You didn't know it was your hand.
cells.verb: to weigh what's owed and give it its true weight
cells.place: the place where something in you is pulling toward what it wants to become
